1. Start here

Most stems in this lecture are solved by a five-part scan: host → geography/exposure → pulmonary pattern → morphology → best test. Treatment is then usually a consequence of the organism and severity.

Host / immune status→Where + what exposure?→Lobar, miliary, diffuse, cavitary, nodular?→Yeast / spherule / hyphae?→Antigen, antibody, culture, histology?

Objective coverage

LO 1
Fungal basics: eukaryotic cell structure, chitin/glucan wall, ergosterol membrane.
LO 2
Yeast vs mold vs dimorphic fungi, including the Coccidioides tissue-form exception.
LO 3a–f
Each required organism: characteristics, culture/stains/serology, pathogenesis, regional distribution, clinical picture, diagnosis, and sequelae.

Professor emphasis: morphology and exposure are repeatedly used to break ties. “Miliary” is not automatically TB; a lung mass is not automatically cancer; and “fungus in an immunocompromised host” is not specific enough.

8. Exam sheet

Part I — Core framework and must-know content

Fungal basics

  • Eukaryotes: membrane-bound nucleus/organelles; 80S ribosomes.
  • Wall: chitin + glucans. Membrane: ergosterol instead of cholesterol.
  • Yeast: single-celled, budding. Mold: hyphae + conidia. Dimorphs: lecture mnemonic “mold in cold, yeast in heat,” with the key Cocci tissue-form exception.
  • Respiratory fungal pathogens are primarily acquired by inhalation; some are endemic, others ubiquitous.

Cryptococcus

Capsulated yeast → immune evasion → lung → CNS. C. neoformans: temperate/pigeons, advanced HIV. C. gattii: eucalyptus/Vancouver and more primary-pathogen behavior. Pulmonary nodules/pneumonia; CNS, skin, bone spread. India ink shows capsule in CSF; CrAg detects capsular polysaccharide. CSF CrAg >95% sensitive in lecture; serum ~60% for isolated pneumonia.

Histoplasma

Ohio/Mississippi valleys + bird/bat guano + small intracellular narrow-based yeast. Environmental mold has tuberculate macroconidia; inhaled microconidia are infectious. TB-like subacute disease, often miliary/reticulonodular. Dissemination → hepatosplenomegaly, marrow/CNS involvement. Antigen = disseminated/high burden; urine concentrates antigen; urine + serum best. Antibody = delayed (~1 month), useful later/chronic.

Blastomyces

Great Lakes/eastern North America + lobar/mass-like pneumonia + broad-based budding yeast. Large 8–15 μm yeast; can disseminate to skin/bone. Verrucous or ulcerative skin lesions. Think “lung cancer mimic.”

Coccidioides

Southwest dust + arthroconidia outside → spherules/endospores inside + eosinophils. Valley fever = self-limited acute pneumonia. Can disseminate to skin, bone, CNS; meningitis may be eosinophilic. Environmental arthroconidia aerosolize readily.

Aspergillus

Septate acute-angle hyphae → angioinvasion → hemorrhage/necrosis → hematogenous emboli. Halo sign = surrounding microhemorrhage. Culture/histopathology emphasized; galactomannan is adjunctive and performance depends on host/burden. Voriconazole is named treatment of choice; surgery/embolization may be needed for destructive/bleeding disease.

Pneumocystis jirovecii

Immunocompromised (AIDS CD4 <200) + subacute dyspnea + diffuse interstitial disease + exertional desaturation. Lacks ergosterol, cannot be routinely cultured. Deep respiratory cytology; LDH and β-D-glucan support. TMP-SMX 21 days; add prednisone if hypoxic.

β-D-glucan — course table

Useful: Aspergillus, Histoplasma, invasive Candida, Pneumocystis. Not helpful: Cryptococcus, Blastomyces, zygomycetes/Mucor/Rhizopus/Absidia. False positives: hemodialysis, beta-lactam antibiotics.

Part II — Distinctions, question-stem decoding, traps

If stem gives…First identify…Then check…Avoid…
Cincinnati + caves + night sweats + miliaryEndemic dimorphSmall intracellular yeast / Histoplasma testing by syndromeCalling miliary = TB automatically
Ontario/Great Lakes + lobar mass + skin lesionBlastomyces patternBroad-based buddingCalling it cancer without tissue morphology
Arizona + dust + eosinophiliaCoccidioidesSpherules/endosporesExpecting budding yeast in tissue
Transplant + necrotic skin nodules + bleeding lesionAngioinvasive moldSeptate acute-angle hyphae / halo signRelying on a nonspecific “fungal test” alone
AIDS + headache + pulmonary nodulesCryptococcus with disseminationCapsule + CSF CrAgUsing negative serum CrAg to rule out pulmonary-only disease
AIDS + diffuse interstitial infiltrates + exertional desaturationPJPDeep respiratory sample, β-D-glucan support, hypoxia severityChoosing an ergosterol-targeting antifungal

Common traps

  • Cocci: “dimorphic” does not mean budding yeast in tissue.
  • Crypto: serum CrAg is not a great lung-only rule-out.
  • Histo: antigen vs antibody depends on burden + time course.
  • Aspergillus: the mechanism is angioinvasion; use that to predict hemorrhage, necrosis, and dissemination.
  • PJP: severe hypoxia changes treatment by adding steroids.

Professor transcript nuances

  • “Miliary” is a radiographic pattern, not a diagnosis.
  • Blastomyces can be discovered during a biopsy done for presumed cancer.
  • Histoplasma mediastinal fibrosis/granulomas/nodules may represent healing sequelae rather than active infection.
  • For Coccidioides, the lecture strongly links eosinophils to both peripheral blood and meningitis.
  • For Aspergillus, obtain a specimen early when possible rather than waiting for a late blood biomarker.

Clarification — Coccidioides transmission: the lecture slide accurately emphasizes that environmental arthroconidia are easily aerosolized and highly infectious. The transcript once uses “contagious” informally; ordinary person-to-person transmission does not occur. CDC: Coccidioidomycosis precautions.
Clarification — Aspergillus galactomannan: the course sources are internally inconsistent about specificity (slide/transcript call it nonspecific in one place; later transcript calls a positive result “really specific”). IDSA treats serum/BAL galactomannan as a useful adjunct whose performance varies by population and sample, with recognized false positives. For this course, keep the professor’s main practical emphasis: culture/histopathology when feasible; biomarker results require context. IDSA Aspergillosis Guideline.

Scope note: this guide intentionally stops at fungal respiratory diseases. The transcript begins to transition to antifungal pharmacology at the end, but no antifungal-pharmacology lecture materials were included in this upload set.
